documents.unit: Office of the Vice Provost for Academic Affairs
documents.title: AI Use Guidelines
documents.summary: The Vice Provost hub page frames Ball State's AI guidelines as living and sets one student expectation: follow the instructor's selected GenAI statement and the Student Academic Ethics Policy. The detailed instructor, research, administrative and misuse guidelines are only linked and were not accessible.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no university-wide stance; it says completion of student checkers "does not automatically mean GenAI use is permitted" and that students "must still follow the GenAI Statement their instructor selected", handing the decision to instructors.

units.why: The page frames the guidelines as helping the community use GenAI "responsibly and ethically", an institution-level statement of purpose and scope, so P56 (framework/preamble) with actor all and general phase; it sets no rule itself.
units.anchor: to help our community use Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools responsibly and ethically

units.why: "These are living guidelines and are continuously updated" says the policy is provisional and will be revised, which is P54 (revisit regularly); informs because it describes the document, not a duty.
units.anchor: These are living guidelines and are continuously updated as new information is received
units.frag_end: All information is subject to change

units.why: "For feedback and questions, please email ai@bsu.edu" invites feedback on the guidelines, which P54 lists ("feedback is invited"); addressed to the whole community.
units.anchor: For feedback and questions, please email
units.frag_start: For feedback and questions, please email

units.anchor: students are encouraged to complete

units.uncovered_note: Students are encouraged to complete institution-provided self-check steps (Should I use AI? How should I use AI responsibly?) covering privacy, integrity, attribution and disclosure before using GenAI on coursework.

units.why: "Completion of the checkers does not automatically mean GenAI use is permitted on every assignment" leaves permission to assignment-level decisions, so P04 (each instructor or assignment sets the rule); P06 does not fit because no fallback is stated.
units.anchor: does not automatically mean GenAI use is permitted on every assignment

units.why: "Students must still follow the GenAI Statement their instructor selected for the course" binds students to the instructor-chosen statement, so P04 (instructor decides); the Statement wording suggests selectable statements but no tiers are described, so not P05.
units.anchor: Students must still follow the GenAI Statement their instructor selected for the course

documents.title: AI Guidelines (AI Initiatives)
documents.summary: Information Technology's AI Guidelines page states seven institutional AI principles, then rules on approved tools, meeting transcription, data classification, retention, sustainability and citation. For coursework it repeats the provost hub and hands the decision to the instructor's GenAI statement.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no course-level stance for student work: it repeats that completion of checkers "does not automatically mean GenAI use is permitted" and that students "must still follow the GenAI Statement their instructor selected". Its own rules concern tools, data and citation, so it delegates.

units.why: The opening says AI has "a profound impact on education, research" and brings challenges that "must be appropriately addressed", an institution-level framing of purpose, so P56.
units.anchor: AI technologies have a profound impact on education, research

units.why: Principle "Excellence" commits to using AI "in ways that align with and uphold our Academic Integrity Policy", a stated institutional principle (P56); the commitment is a principle, not a rule on a specific use.
units.anchor: We commit to using AI in ways that align with and uphold our

units.why: Principle "Innovation" commits to "responsible AI experimentation and implementation to enhance creativity, learning, and research", welcoming AI use; framework statement so P56 (P02 would be a default stance for a course, which this is not).
units.anchor: responsible AI experimentation and implementation to enhance creativity, learning, and research

units.why: Principle "Courage" commits to "exploring the possibilities within AI while also addressing potential ethical challenges and risks", an institution-level principle (P56).
units.anchor: willingly exploring the possibilities within AI while also addressing potential ethical challenges and risks

units.why: Principle "Integrity" commits to "upholding human creativity and critical thinking with our AI usage, avoiding misuse"; this expects humans to remain the thinkers, closest to P32 (students stay primary problem-solver) though stated institution-wide.
units.anchor: upholding human creativity and critical thinking with our AI usage, avoiding misuse

units.why: Principle "Inclusiveness" commits to "developing and using AI in accessible and equitable ways", an equity and access commitment (P51).
units.anchor: developing and using AI in accessible and equitable ways

units.why: Principle "Social responsibility" commits to "minimizing harm, maintaining rigorous standards, and prioritizing ethical considerations", naming ethical concerns about AI (P53).
units.anchor: minimizing harm, maintaining rigorous standards, and prioritizing ethical considerations when using AI

units.why: Principle "Gratitude" commits to "valuing collaboration and appreciating the ethical guidelines that shape responsible AI use", another institution-level principle (P56).

documents.unit: Office of the Vice Provost, Student Services
documents.title: Academic Integrity Policy
documents.summary: The Academic Integrity page is mostly a general misconduct process. Its AI content tells faculty to state generative-AI expectations on syllabi, points to the Student and Faculty AI guidelines, and recommends two AI-use scales to communicate levels of acceptable use.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no AI stance. It asks faculty to "make explicit on your syllabi ... using generative AI (for the entire course or for specific assignments)", so the rule is left to instructors and courses.

units.why: The Faculty section tells instructors to "Make explicit on your syllabi ... your expectations" including "using generative AI", requiring an AI statement in the syllabus, so P09.
units.anchor: Make explicit on your syllabi and discuss with students your expectations

units.why: "for the entire course or for specific assignments" shows the AI rule may be set at either level by the instructor, which is P04 (instructor or assignment sets the rule).
units.anchor: entire course or for specific assignments

units.why: Step 1 tells instructors to hold a "preliminary inquiry meeting" before deciding whether a formal allegation is warranted and points to the "Guidelines for Instructors to Address Suspected AI Misuse"; the process is generic but applies to AI cases, so P57 (talk with the student before escalating).
units.anchor: meet to discuss incident before instructor determines whether a formal allegation is warranted

units.why: Students are told to "Know when AI tools are permissible and how to properly cite them", which asks students to learn the permission rules and to cite AI use (P24).
units.anchor: Know when AI tools are permissible and how to properly cite them.
units.frag_start: Know when AI tools are permissible

units.why: The page recommends the "Student Generative AI Use Scale" and "AI Assessment Scale" for "communicating to students the varying levels of acceptable AI use", i.e. named levels of AI use, so P05.
units.anchor: communicating to students the varying levels of acceptable AI use
units.frag_start: The Student Generative AI Use Scale

units.why: "there is a lot of discussion about the different ways AI can enable and disrupt learning" is a framing statement on why AI matters to teaching; P56 (preamble) is the nearest type.
units.anchor: different ways AI can enable and disrupt learning for many students

notes: Coder A. The detailed instructor, research, administrative and misuse guidelines are on an inaccessible SharePoint PDF, so they are not coded. The generic academic-ethics process (deadlines, hearing panel, sanctions up to failure, suspension, expulsion) is not AI-specific and was not coded except one P57 unit, because the page only links the AI-misuse guidelines. Pages repeat the hub text, and each document was coded on its own. The task named no topic list (AGENT_BRIEF.md absent), so topics use free kebab-case labels.
